blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+
+Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
+- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).

+A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

+/**
+ * quotaCircuitBreaker.js — gh-1087 quota circuit-breaker (pure logic, no dmtools globals).

+ * A hard provider-quota failure (HTTP 403 usage-limit / billing body — e.g.
+ * "weekly (7-day) usage limit" — or a "Provider chain exhausted" tail that
+ * follows quota responses) must PARK the leg lane instead of burning a
+ * per-tick retry against a wall that cannot succeed until the quota window
+ * resets. Transient interruptions (429 rate-limit blips, timeouts, network

+ *   probeDue(priorCount, everyN)       → is a probe due this tick?
+ *   probeMarkerLine(n)                 → durable per-ticket probe counter line
+ *   countProbeMarkers(bodies)          → probe attempts already recorded

1. **BLOCKING** — probe cadence deadlock in `probeDue`/`countProbeMarkers`. The counter only advances when a probe fires, so after probe #1 (`quota-probe: 1`), the count is 1 forever and `1 % 3 !== 0` → probe #2 never fires. Reviewer suggested option 1: post a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker each tick and probe when `n % everyN === 0`. I need to pick an option. Also add an integration test running `quotaParkProbe.action` for at least 2×everyN consecutive failing ticks asserting a second probe fires.

Likely the flagged function is one of the new/changed high-branch functions: `quotaParkProbe.js#action`, `completeInterruptedPath`, `parkQuotaExhaustedDevelopment`. CRAP threshold is 8. Since coverage reduces CRAP, functions with many branches but uncovered branches would be flagged. Actually CRAP = complexity²·(1-coverage)³ + complexity. New functions above threshold 8 fail. blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \

Key facts:
- EPSILON 0.5: regression = score > before + 0.5. So a small CC +1 growth on a low-CC function (e.g. CC 2→3, CRAP 2→3) is a regression of 1.0 > 0.5 → fails. On a mid function +1 CC could be < 0.5 epsilon if coverage high? CRAP delta for +1 CC with full cov = 1 → regression. So any CC growth on covered functions fails. But for functions with low coverage, CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC; +1 CC change could be large.
- Only functions with CRAP > 8 (when threshold=8... wait, baseline only records functions with crapScore > threshold). Regressions are checked only for keys present in baseline — i.e., functions whose MAIN-side CRAP was > 8. Functions at/below 8 on main are absent from the baseline; on the PR they're "new" and must be ≤ 8... but with EPSILON: `if (score > threshold) newOverThreshold.push` — strictly > 8.
- So: existing functions with main CRAP ≤ 8 can drift up to exactly 8.0. Existing functions with main CRAP > 8 must not grow more than +0.5.
- New functions must be ≤ 8.0 (strictly; 8.0 passes, 8.1 fails).

Now measure main. Build a main worktree, instrument, run coverage, build baseline with threshold 8, then compare head metrics against it.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository …

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

Key facts:
- EPSILON 0.5: regression = score > before + 0.5. So a small CC +1 growth on a low-CC function (e.g. CC 2→3, CRAP 2→3) is a regression of 1.0 > 0.5 → fails. On a mid function +1 CC could be < 0.5 epsilon if coverage high? CRAP delta for +1 CC with full cov = 1 → regression. So any CC growth on covered functions fails. But for functions with low coverage, CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC; +1 CC change could be large.
- Only functions with CRAP > 8 (when threshold=8... wait, baseline only records functions with crapScore > threshold). Regressions are checked only for keys present in baseline — i.e., functions whose MAIN-side CRAP was > 8. Functions at/below 8 on main are absent from the baseline; on the PR they're "new" and must be ≤ 8... but with EPSILON: `if (score > threshold) newOverThreshold.push` — strictly > 8.
- So: existing functions with main CRAP ≤ 8 can drift up to exactly 8.0. Existing functions with main CRAP > 8 must not grow more than +0.5.
- New functions must be ≤ 8.0 (strictly; 8.0 passes, 8.1 fails).

+# Quota Park Probe
+
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+
+## Parameters
+

Key facts:
- EPSILON 0.5: regression = score > before + 0.5. So a small CC +1 growth on a low-CC function (e.g. CC 2→3, CRAP 2→3) is a regression of 1.0 > 0.5 → fails. On a mid function +1 CC could be < 0.5 epsilon if coverage high? CRAP delta for +1 CC with full cov = 1 → regression. So any CC growth on covered functions fails. But for functions with low coverage, CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC; +1 CC change could be large.
- Only functions with CRAP > 8 (when threshold=8... wait, baseline only records functions with crapScore > threshold). Regressions are checked only for keys present in baseline — i.e., functions whose MAIN-side CRAP was > 8. Functions at/below 8 on main are absent from the baseline; on the PR they're "new" and must be ≤ 8... but with EPSILON: `if (score > threshold) newOverThreshold.push` — strictly > 8.
- So: existing functions with main CRAP ≤ 8 can drift up to exactly 8.0. Existing functions with main CRAP > 8 must not grow more than +0.5.
- New functions must be ≤ 8.0 (strictly; 8.0 passes, 8.1 fails).

1. **BLOCKING** — probe cadence deadlock in `probeDue`/`countProbeMarkers`. The counter only advances when a probe fires, so after probe #1 (`quota-probe: 1`), the count is 1 forever and `1 % 3 !== 0` → probe #2 never fires. Reviewer suggested option 1: post a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker each tick and probe when `n % everyN === 0`. I need to pick an option. Also add an integration test running `quotaParkProbe.action` for at least 2×everyN consecutive failing ticks asserting a second probe fires.

Likely the flagged function is one of the new/changed high-branch functions: `quotaParkProbe.js#action`, `completeInterruptedPath`, `parkQuotaExhaustedDevelopment`. CRAP threshold is 8. Since coverage reduces CRAP, functions with many branches but uncovered branches would be flagged. Actually CRAP = complexity²·(1-coverage)³ + complexity. New functions above threshold 8 fail. Let me try to run crap4js locally if possible? Probably network access needed (npm install from GitHub). Let me check if network is available. Key facts:
- EPSILON 0.5: regression = score > before + 0.5. So a small CC +1 growth on a low-CC function (e.g. CC 2→3, CRAP 2→3) is a regression of 1.0 > 0.5 → fails. On a mid function +1 CC could be < 0.5 epsilon if coverage high? CRAP delta for +1 CC with full cov = 1 → regression. So any CC growth on covered functions fails. But for functions with low coverage, CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC; +1 CC change could be large.
- Only functions with CRAP > 8 (when threshold=8... wait, baseline only records functions with crapScore > threshold). Regressions are checked only for keys present in baseline — i.e., functions whose MAIN-side CRAP was > 8. Functions at/below 8 on main are absent from the baseline; on the PR they're "new" and must be ≤ 8... but with EPSILON: `if (score > threshold) newOverThreshold.push` — strictly > 8.
- So: existing functions with main CRAP ≤ 8 can drift up to exactly 8.0. Existing functions with main CRAP > 8 must not grow more than +0.5.
- New functions must be ≤ 8.0 (strictly; 8.0 passes, 8.1 fails).

messages.preview: The regex needs to swallow `Bearer ` with the token (otherwise it masks "Bearer" and leaks the key):

blocks.text:
Wait — SENSITIVE_VALUE_RE: for the default command, the text contains `Authorization: Bearer $FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY`. My regex: `((?:authorization|...)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*"?)([^'"\s]+)("?)`. Match: prefix = `Authorization: `, value = `Bearer`, suffix = ``. Hmm — `[^'"\s]+` stops at whitespace → value = "Bearer", not the token! Then it would redact "Bearer" → "Authorization: ***" and leave `$FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` exposed (env ref, safe anyway). But the test asserts `redactCommand(dflt) === dflt`. With my regex, `Bearer` doesn't start with $ → masked → test fails. Also for the real leak case: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...` → value = "Bearer" → masked to `Authorization: *** sk-live-...` — the actual key leaks! Bad regex.

Fix: match `Bearer\s+\S+` as a unit. Better regex: 
```
/(authorization|x-api-key|api[-_]?key|token|secret)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*(?:"?Bearer\s+)?"?([^\s'"]+)("?)/gi
```
and treat the whole value (including Bearer prefix). Let me restructure: capture prefix up to and including the optional `Bearer `, then the token:

[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]
var SENSITIVE_VALUE_RE = /((?:authorization|x-api-key|api[-_]?key|token|secret)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*(?:bearer\s+)?"?)([^\s'"]+)("?)/gi;
```
For `Authorization: Bearer $FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY`: prefix=`Authorization: Bearer `, value=`$FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` → ENV_REF → keep. ✓ dflt unchanged... wait also `Content-Type:` header — not sensitive ✓. But `-d "{\"model\":\"$FA_PROVIDER_MODEL...` — contains `token` hmm: "max_tokens\":1" — does `token[\w-]*\s*[:=]` match `"max_tokens\":`? `max_tokens` contains "token"... my regex looks for `(?:authorization|x-api-key|api[-_]?key|token|secret)[\w-]*\s*[:=]` — "max_tokens\":" → "token" followed by `s` (in [\w-]*) then `\":"` — after `[\w-]*` we need `\s*[:=]` — next char is `"` not `:` → no match at that position. What about `max_tokens\":1`? After "max_tokens" comes `\"` then `:`. `\s*` matches empty, then needs `:` but finds `"` → no match ✓. Hmm wait, but regex could match starting at "tokens\":1"? Still the quote blocks. OK.

But `"content\":\"ping\"` fine. `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` — preceded by `$`: `(?:...api[-_]?key...)` — "API_KEY" matches `api[-_]?key`? Case-insensitive: "API_KEY" → `api` + `[-_]?` matches `_`? "API_KEY" = A P I _ K E Y: api matches API, [-_]? matches _, key matches KEY ✓. Then `[\w-]*` empty, `\s*[:=]` — next char after KEY is `"` (it's `\"$FA...`) wait the default command: `-H "Authorization: Bearer $FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY"` — FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY followed by `"`. After matching "API_KEY", next char `"` ≠ [:=] → no match ✓ good.

For `--api-key=AKIA...`: prefix `--api-key=`, hmm my regex has no boundary for `-` before: `(?:...api[-_]?key...)` matches "api-key" inside "--api-key": the preceding `--` are just characters before match. prefix=`--api-key=`? Let me see: match starts at "api-key=[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" with prefix group = "api-key="[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]"[REDACTED:AWS Access Key]" → masked ✓. suffix group `("?)` matches empty. Result: `--***=***`? No — the prefix INCLUDES the match start "api-key="[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]"api"). Preceding "--" remain. Result: `--` + `api-key=***`. Good, test asserts notContains AKIA ✓ and contains `***` ✓.

For `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...`: prefix = `Authorization: Bearer ` (with optional bearer consumed), value = `sk-live-1234567890abcdef` → masked → `Authorization: Bearer ***`? My test asserts contains 'Authorization: ***' — with Bearer kept in prefix, result is 'Authorization: Bearer ***' which does NOT contain 'Authorization: ***'. Fix test or strip Bearer. I'll keep Bearer in the prefix and update the test expectation to 'Bearer ***'. Also the probe-log test asserts joined contains 'Authorization: ***' — update both to 'Bearer ***'.

Also quoted case: `-H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..."` — prefix includes opening quote? My prefix has optional `"?` before value... the quote after -H and space: `-H "Authorization:` — the `"` comes BEFORE "Authorization", not captured in prefix — remains in output ✓. Trailing `"` after token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] `("?)` captures it ✓.

Now update the regex and the two test assertions.
The regex needs to swallow `Bearer ` with the token (otherwise it masks "Bearer" and leaks the key):

On a mid function +1 CC could be < 0.5 epsilon if coverage high? CRAP delta for +1 CC with full cov = 1 → regression. So any CC growth on covered functions fails. But for functions with low coverage, CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC; +1 CC change could be large.
- Only functions with CRAP > 8 (when threshold=8... wait, baseline only records functions with crapScore > threshold). Regressions are checked only for keys present in baseline — i.e., functions whose MAIN-side CRAP was > 8. Functions at/below 8 on main are absent from the baseline; on the PR they're "new" and must be ≤ 8... but with EPSILON: `if (score > threshold) newOverThreshold.push` — strictly > 8.
- So: existing functions with main CRAP ≤ 8 can drift up to exactly 8.0. Existing functions with main CRAP > 8 must not grow more than +0.5.
- New functions must be ≤ 8.0 (strictly; 8.0 passes, 8.1 fails).
```

Key facts:
- EPSILON 0.5: regression = score > before + 0.5. So a small CC +1 growth on a low-CC function (e.g. CC 2→3, CRAP 2→3) is a regression of 1.0 > 0.5 → fails. On a mid function +1 CC could be < 0.5 epsilon if coverage high? CRAP delta for +1 CC with full cov = 1 → regression. So any CC growth on covered functions fails. But for functions with low coverage, CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC; +1 CC change could be large.
- Only functions with CRAP > 8 (when threshold=8... wait, baseline only records functions with crapScore > threshold). Regressions are checked only for keys present in baseline — i.e., functions whose MAIN-side CRAP was > 8. Functions at/below 8 on main are absent from the baseline; on the PR they're "new" and must be ≤ 8... but with EPSILON: `if (score > threshold) newOverThreshold.push` — strictly > 8.
- So: existing functions with main CRAP ≤ 8 can drift up to exactly 8.0. Existing functions with main CRAP > 8 must not grow more than +0.5.
- New functions must be ≤ 8.0 (strictly; 8.0 passes, 8.1 fails).

```
Key facts:
- EPSILON 0.5: regression = score > before + 0.5. So a small CC +1 growth on a low-CC function (e.g. CC 2→3, CRAP 2→3) is a regression of 1.0 > 0.5 → fails. On a mid function +1 CC could be < 0.5 epsilon if coverage high? CRAP delta for +1 CC with full cov = 1 → regression. So any CC growth on covered functions fails. But for functions with low coverage, CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC; +1 CC change could be large.
- Only functions with CRAP > 8 (when threshold=8... wait, baseline only records functions with crapScore > threshold). Regressions are checked only for keys present in baseline — i.e., functions whose MAIN-side CRAP was > 8. Functions at/below 8 on main are absent from the baseline; on the PR they're "new" and must be ≤ 8... but with EPSILON: `if (score > threshold) newOverThreshold.push` — strictly > 8.
- So: existing functions with main CRAP ≤ 8 can drift up to exactly 8.0. Existing functions with main CRAP > 8 must not grow more than +0.5.
- New functions must be ≤ 8.0 (strictly; 8.0 passes, 8.1 fails).

Now measure main. Build a main worktree, instrument, run coverage, build baseline with threshold 8, then compare head metrics against it.
```

Key facts:
- EPSILON 0.5: regression = score > before + 0.5. So a small CC +1 growth on a low-CC function (e.g. CC 2→3, CRAP 2→3) is a regression of 1.0 > 0.5 → fails. On a mid function +1 CC could be < 0.5 epsilon if coverage high? CRAP delta for +1 CC with full cov = 1 → regression. So any CC growth on covered functions fails. But for functions with low coverage, CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC; +1 CC change could be large.
- Only functions with CRAP > 8 (when threshold=8... wait, baseline only records functions with crapScore > threshold). Regressions are checked only for keys present in baseline — i.e., functions whose MAIN-side CRAP was > 8. Functions at/below 8 on main are absent from the baseline; on the PR they're "new" and must be ≤ 8... but with EPSILON: `if (score > threshold) newOverThreshold.push` — strictly > 8.
- So: existing functions with main CRAP ≤ 8 can drift up to exactly 8.0. Existing functions with main CRAP > 8 must not grow more than +0.5.
- New functions must be ≤ 8.0 (strictly; 8.0 passes, 8.1 fails).

messages.preview: The regex needs to swallow `Bearer ` with the token (otherwise it masks "Bearer" and leaks the key):

blocks.text:
Wait — SENSITIVE_VALUE_RE: for the default command, the text contains `Authorization: Bearer $FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY`. My regex: `((?:authorization|...)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*"?)([^'"\s]+)("?)`. Match: prefix = `Authorization: `, value = `Bearer`, suffix = ``. Hmm — `[^'"\s]+` stops at whitespace → value = "Bearer", not the token! Then it would redact "Bearer" → "Authorization: ***" and leave `$FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` exposed (env ref, safe anyway). But the test asserts `redactCommand(dflt) === dflt`. With my regex, `Bearer` doesn't start with $ → masked → test fails. Also for the real leak case: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...` → value = "Bearer" → masked to `Authorization: *** sk-live-...` — the actual key leaks! Bad regex.

Fix: match `Bearer\s+\S+` as a unit. Better regex: 
```
/(authorization|x-api-key|api[-_]?key|token|secret)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*(?:"?Bearer\s+)?"?([^\s'"]+)("?)/gi
```
```

# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

Wait — SENSITIVE_VALUE_RE: for the default command, the text contains `Authorization: Bearer $FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY`. My regex: `((?:authorization|...)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*"?)([^'"\s]+)("?)`. Match: prefix = `Authorization: `, value = `Bearer`, suffix = ``. Hmm — `[^'"\s]+` stops at whitespace → value = "Bearer", not the token! Then it would redact "Bearer" → "Authorization: ***" and leave `$FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` exposed (env ref, safe anyway). But the test asserts `redactCommand(dflt) === dflt`. With my regex, `Bearer` doesn't start with $ → masked → test fails. Also for the real leak case: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...` → value = "Bearer" → masked to `Authorization: *** sk-live-...` — the actual key leaks! Bad regex.

Fix: match `Bearer\s+\S+` as a unit. Better regex: 
```
/(authorization|x-api-key|api[-_]?key|token|secret)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*(?:"?Bearer\s+)?"?([^\s'"]+)("?)/gi
```
and treat the whole value (including Bearer prefix). Let me restructure: capture prefix up to and including the optional `Bearer `, then the token:

```

{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

```
{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.
```

{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

```
{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.
```

{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.
","path":"docs/agents/quota_park_probe.md"}

 # Quota Park Probe
 
-Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded probe count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
+Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).
 
-Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a one-line `quota-probe: <n>` marker comment that doubles as the durable counter for the next tick's cadence decision.
+Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).
 
 ## Parameters
 
 - `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
 - `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
-- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes.

Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.
 
 A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

messages.preview: The regex needs to swallow `Bearer ` with the token (otherwise it masks "Bearer" and leaks the key):

blocks.text:
Wait — SENSITIVE_VALUE_RE: for the default command, the text contains `Authorization: Bearer $FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY`. My regex: `((?:authorization|...)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*"?)([^'"\s]+)("?)`. Match: prefix = `Authorization: `, value = `Bearer`, suffix = ``. Hmm — `[^'"\s]+` stops at whitespace → value = "Bearer", not the token! Then it would redact "Bearer" → "Authorization: ***" and leave `$FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` exposed (env ref, safe anyway). But the test asserts `redactCommand(dflt) === dflt`. With my regex, `Bearer` doesn't start with $ → masked → test fails. Also for the real leak case: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...` → value = "Bearer" → masked to `Authorization: *** sk-live-...` — the actual key leaks! Bad regex.

Fix: match `Bearer\s+\S+` as a unit. Better regex: 
```
/(authorization|x-api-key|api[-_]?key|token|secret)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*(?:"?Bearer\s+)?"?([^\s'"]+)("?)/gi
```
and treat the whole value (including Bearer prefix). Let me restructure: capture prefix up to and including the optional `Bearer `, then the token:

[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]
var SENSITIVE_VALUE_RE = /((?:authorization|x-api-key|api[-_]?key|token|secret)[\w-]*\s*[:=]\s*(?:bearer\s+)?"?)([^\s'"]+)("?)/gi;
```

{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.
```

{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.
","path":"docs/agents/quota_park_probe.md"}

```
{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.
```

{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.

arguments.content:
## Issues/Notes

- **BLOCKING (review thread 1) — probe cadence deadlock, confirmed and reproduced.** The shipped cadence was attempts-only: `probeDue(priorProbeCount, everyN)` fired only when the recorded probe count was a multiple of N, and the count (`countProbeMarkers`) advanced only when a probe fired. After failed probe #1 the count was stuck at 1 forever (`1 % 3 !== 0`), so probe #2 could never fire — the park never self-lifts (AC3 broken). Reproduced in RED first: a new integration test driving `quotaParkProbe.action` over 7 consecutive failing SM ticks (cadence 3) fired exactly **one** probe before the fix.
- **CI `crap` check failure (log not fetchable).** Reproduced locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201` + `nyc` instrumented run against an `origin/main` baseline: **2 regressions** (`developBugAndCreatePR.js::completeInterruptedPath` 8→12, `developBugAndCreatePR.js::action` 23.7→27.9) and **6 new functions over the CRAP-threshold 8** (`classifyFailure` 13, `quotaParkProbe.js::action` 24.8, `shouldSkipForQuotaPark` 9.2, `recoverMissingResponse` 9, `parkQuotaPath` 8.8, `parkQuotaExhaustedDevelopment` 8.6).
- **SUGGESTION (review thread 2) — probe command logged verbatim.** An operator override of `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` with an inline credential would land in SM job logs / CI artifacts.

## Approach

1. **Cadence fix (reviewer's option 1 — record every tick).** New durable per-tick clock: `quotaParkProbe.action` posts a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker **every** SM tick, so the completed-tick count advances even between probes. `probeDue(completedTicks, everyN)` now fires when the completed tick count is a multiple of N — probes recur on ticks 1, N+1, 2N+1, … while the provider stays quota-blocked. `quota-probe: <n>` markers remain but drive probe *numbering* only. New pure functions in `js/common/quotaCircuitBreaker.js`: `tickMarkerLine`, `countTickMarkers`, shared `maxMarkerNumber`, plus `redactCommand`.

{"content":"# quota park probe

Bounded self-lift for the gh-1087 provider-quota park: runs locally on every SM tick against tickets carrying the park label (default `provider_quota`) and fires one cheap provider ping only when the recorded park-tick count hits the `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` cadence (default 3 ticks).

Every tick records a lightweight `quota-park-tick: n` marker comment — the durable cadence clock — so the tick count advances even between probes (an attempts-only counter deadlocks after the first failed probe: probe #2 can never fire). Probe success means the quota window has reset or the provider was reconfigured — the handler removes the park label, clears the development/rework dispatch trigger labels, moves the ticket back to Ready For Development and posts an un-park comment, so the normal dispatch lanes resume on the next tick. Probe failure keeps the park and posts a `quota-probe: <n>` marker used for probe numbering only. The probe command is logged redacted (sensitive header/credential values masked, env-var name references untouched).

## Parameters

- `jobParams.quotaParkLabel` — park label name to watch and remove (default `provider_quota`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = provider_quota`) must be overridden to match.
- `jobParams.quotaProbeEveryNTicks` — probe cadence in SM ticks (default 3). The first tick after the park always probes (a misclassification self-corrects immediately).
- `jobParams.quotaProbeCommand` — the cheap provider ping shell command (default: a 1-token chat completion against the fa provider config `FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` / `FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY` / `FA_PROVIDER_MODEL`; curl `--fail` keeps the park on any HTTP error). Override for non-fa provider shapes. The command is logged in redacted form — inline credentials are masked.

A human un-parks immediately by removing the park label from the ticket — the probe rule stops matching and no further probes fire.
","path":"docs/agents/quota_park_probe.md"}
